consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has astigmatism, which means he has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up. It's been a challenge for him in school, especially during lessons that involve a lot of writing on the board.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't quite catch what they said the first time. It's not that he can't hear well; it's more about processing the sound into understandable language quickly enough.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth have weak enamel, which makes them prone to cavities and sensitivity. We've had to be very diligent about his dental care and regular check-ups to prevent any major issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's an abnormality with one of his heart valves. Thankfully, it hasn't affected his energy levels or ability to play with friends yet, but we do have to go back for frequent check-ups to monitor the situation closely.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He was born with a tethered cord condition. While it's not caused significant mobility issues or anything drastic, we do keep an eye on how it might affect him long-term.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He's always been a bit slow to gain weight compared to his peers. Not drastically underweight or anything alarming, just a steady observation over time that he doesn't seem to put on pounds as quickly as others his age.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Sometimes he struggles with finding the right words when trying to speak. It's almost as if he knows what he wants to say but can't get it out clearly. This has been noticeable especially during conversations that require complex thoughts or explanations.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Asthma susceptibility
- Need for regular ENT check-ups
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Increased risk of respiratory infections
- Potential need for prolonged ENT interventions

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Heart valve abnormalities requiring follow-up
- Possible need for pacemaker insertion
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of congenital heart defects
- Higher likelihood of arrhythmias and valve-related issues

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Delayed gastric emptying leading to feeding difficulties
- Risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Frequent occurrence of GI complications
- Greater susceptibility to GERD and delayed gastric emptying

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Susceptibility to viral infections
- Potential need for immunotherapy
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- High prevalence of autoimmune disorders
- Increased vulnerability to infectious diseases

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Neurodevelopmental delays affecting fine motor skills
- Speech and language challenges
- Behavioral differences
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Consistent presentation of neurodevelopmental variability
- Variable severity of behavioral and cognitive impairments

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Otitis media with effusion requiring tube insertions
- Nasal congestion impacting sleep and comfort
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Prevalence of chronic sinusitis and nasal polyps
- Increased risk of otitis media and adenoid hypertrophy

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Vision problems including astigmatism and short-sightedness
- Need for regular eye examinations
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- High incidence of ocular anomalies
- Greater susceptibility to visual disturbances

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Skin pigmentation variations
- Prone to eczema flare-ups
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common presentation of skin anomalies
- Increased likelihood of dermatological issues

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Stronger tooth enamel requiring meticulous dental care
- Increased frequency of dental procedures
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- High prevalence of dental anomalies
- Greater susceptibility to caries and gum disease

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Requires additional educational support
- May struggle with social interactions
- Needs tailored curriculum adaptations
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Consistent requirement for specialized educational provision
- Potential for social integration challenges

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulties with communication and empathy
- Potential for behavioral regression
- Requires targeted therapeutic intervention
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Consistent presentation of behavioral and cognitive heterogeneity
- Variable outcomes in terms of adaptive behavior and emotional regulation

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Skeletal anomalies like brachydactyly and clinodactyly
- Increased risk of skeletal deformities
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Prevalence of skeletal dysmorphisms
- Higher likelihood of musculoskeletal issues

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups
- Monitoring for heart valve abnormalities
- Consideration for cardiac MRI if clinical concerns arise
- Regular ENT check-ups and possible tube insertions
- Management of asthma and allergies
- Speech therapy and occupational therapy
- Behavioural therapy and counseling
- Orthodontic evaluation for potential treatment needs
- Follow-up for tethered cord condition
- Regular physical examination for hormonal imbalances
- Monitoring for gastrointestinal issues
- Nutritional assessment and dietary modifications
- Immunotherapy as indicated
- Genetic counseling and testing for family members
- Long-term follow-up for neurological and cardiovascular concerns

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected respiratory issues due to hypotonia affecting chest wall strength and potentially contributing to nasal regurgitation.
- Possible airway concerns due to anatomical variations noted in the consultation.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia is a common feature associated with KBG syndrome, impacting respiratory strength and airway patency.
- Anatomical variations such as a triangular-shaped face and synophrys can contribute to potential airway concerns.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected valvular abnormalities due to the congenital heart defect mentioned.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Valvular abnormalities are commonly observed in KBG syndrome, contributing to heart-related concerns.
- Congenital heart defects are frequent in this population, warranting thorough cardiac evaluations.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected feeding difficulties and possible swallowing issues due to hypotonia affecting oral-motor function.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia impacts oral-motor function, leading to challenges with feeding and possibly swallowing.
- Swallowing difficulties can increase the risk of aspiration pneumonia, a concern in KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Immune system dysfunction is uncommon in KBG syndrome, but occasional reports suggest susceptibility to infections.
- Given the variability in immune responses, ongoing surveillance and consideration of prophylactic vaccinations are advised.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected hypotonia affecting muscle tone and coordination.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia is a hallmark feature of KBG syndrome, impacting motor development and overall neuromuscular function.
- Coordination and balance issues can lead to falls and other injuries, requiring careful home safety considerations.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected feeding difficulties and possible swallowing issues due to hypotonia affecting oral-motor function.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia impacts oral-motor function, leading to challenges with feeding and possibly swallowing.
- Swallowing difficulties can increase the risk of aspiration pneumonia, a concern in KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected palatal anomalies affecting speech and feeding.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Palatal anomalies are frequently observed in KBG syndrome, impacting speech and feeding capabilities.
- Ongoing monitoring and consideration of orthodontic interventions may be warranted.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skin manifestations are generally mild and non-specific in KBG syndrome, making dermatological evaluation routine rather than diagnostic.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected feeding difficulties and possible swallowing issues due to hypotonia affecting oral-motor function.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hypotonia impacts oral-motor function, leading to challenges with feeding and possibly swallowing.
- Feeding difficulties can necessitate dietary modifications and specialized feeding techniques.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- Potential educational delays and behavioral differences impact academic performance and social interactions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic delays and behavioral differences are consistent features of KBG syndrome, influencing educational outcomes and social adaptation.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are highly variable but commonly reported in KBG syndrome, affecting social interaction, emotional regulation, and cognitive abilities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- Suspected skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly and clinodactyly, and an unusual structure of spinal bones.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies are frequent in KBG syndrome, contributing to musculoskeletal concerns such as scoliosis and weak tooth enamel.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups to address feeding difficulties and possible swallowing issues.
- Monitoring for thyroid gland involvement, given the prevalence of hypothyroidism in KBG syndrome.
- Speech therapy to address feeding and speech development challenges.
- Orthodontic intervention for suspected craniosynostosis or other skeletal anomalies.
- Consideration of growth hormone therapy for taller siblings or younger relatives with similar chromosomal deletions.
- Regular cardiovascular assessments, including echocardiograms and ECGs, to monitor for heart defects.
- Management of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with medications and dietary adjustments.
- Referral for pediatric neurology consultations for ongoing neurological evaluations and management of hypotonia.
- Genetic counseling and testing for family members, considering the autosomal dominant nature of the condition.
- Regular ophthalmology appointments to monitor vision and address any ocular concerns.
- Consideration of behavioral therapy and educational supports tailored to the patient's needs.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... he sits way too close to the TV and books. I'm constantly reminding him to move back, worried it might affect his eyesight. It's like he can't see things clearly unless they're right in front of him.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes I call his name, and he doesn't respond. Not always‚ but often enough that it worries me. I've taken him to get his hearing checked‚ and everything seems fine‚ but still... it's unsettling when he doesn't answer.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are my biggest worry! They chip or break so easily. We've had to take him to the dentist more times than I can count‚ and it's always something new. I'm at my wit's end trying to figure out how to protect them better.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... his heart. The doctors said we need to monitor it closely‚ so we go for regular check-ups. It's reassuring that they're keeping an eye on it‚ but the thought of anything going wrong is always lurking.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: The hypotonia is our main concern. His muscles seem too weak sometimes‚ and it affects his movements and balance. We're working with therapists to help strengthen them‚ but it's slow progress.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures are a nightmare! He's extremely picky‚ refusing to eat anything with certain feels or looks. Mealtime is stressful‚ trying to find something‚ anything‚ he'll tolerate.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Speech is another big issue. He doesn't speak as much as other kids his age‚ and even when he tries‚ it's hard for others to understand him. We're in speech therapy‚ but progress is slow. It breaks my heart seeing him struggle to express himself.

a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of heart valve abnormalities requiring monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Heart valve abnormalities are commonly associated with KBG syndrome, increasing the risk of infective endocarditis and valvular regurgitation.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has experienced episodes of glue ear, which can lead to temporary hearing loss and potential speech delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Glue ear is a frequent complication in children with KBG syndrome, potentially affecting speech development and hearing.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, including Type 1 diabetes mellitus and inflammatory bowel disease.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits developmental delays, behavioral differences, and a characteristic facial appearance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, contributing to challenges in social interactions and emotional regulation.

a) How this affects the patient:

a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of vision problems, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

a) How this affects the patient:

- Dermatological manifestations are uncommon in children with KBG syndrome, making skin assessments routine rather than specific.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires careful toothbrushing and dietary modifications to prevent enamel weakening.

a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has shown variability in educational outcomes, ranging from successful integration into mainstream education to specialized placements.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections, particularly during cold seasons.
- There is a history of recurrent otitis media requiring multiple grommet insertions.
- The patient has a slightly enlarged tonsil size compared to peers without KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Recurrent otitis media and adenoid hypertrophy are frequent complications in KBG syndrome.
- Enlarged tonsils can lead to difficulty breathing during sleep and snoring.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires periodic cardiac evaluations, including echocardiography and ECG monitoring.
- The presence of heart valve abnormalities and congenital heart defects has been documented in some KBG syndrome patients.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Heart murmurs and structural heart defects are commonly associated with KBG syndrome.
- Regular cardiovascular assessments are crucial for early detection and intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits feeding difficulties, characterized by selective eating habits and reluctance to try new foods.
- There is a reported incidence of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Selective eating patterns and dietary restrictions are frequent observations in KBG syndrome.
- GERD is a common gastrointestinal issue affecting many individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has experienced seizure activity, necessitating medication management.
- The occurrence of febrile seizures is relatively high among KBG syndrome patients.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Febrile seizures are a known complication in KBG syndrome, warranting vigilance and appropriate treatment.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient displays behavioral differences, including autistic traits and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
- The presence of synophrys (synclitism) contributes to the distinctive facial appearance.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, impacting social interactions and emotional regulation.
- Synphrys contribute to the unique facial phenotype observed in KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of glue ear requiring multiple grommet insertions.
- There is a noted sensitivity to cold temperatures, indicating potential involvement of the nasal passages.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Glue ear and anosmia (loss of smell) are common complications in KBG syndrome.
- Sensitivity to cold temperatures suggests possible involvement of the nasal cavity.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of vision-related issues, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems, such as astigmatism and short-sightedness, are frequent in KBG syndrome.
- Regular ophthalmological examinations are essential for managing these ocular concerns.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits a distinct facial appearance, characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-spaced eyes, and thick eyebrows.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The characteristic facial features are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has selective eating habits, leading to potential nutritional deficiencies.
- Dental issues, such as weak enamel and tooth sensitivity, are observed.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Selective eating patterns and dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome.
- Regular dental care and monitoring for enamel hypoplasia are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires additional educational support, including accommodations and interventions tailored to address their specific needs.
- Transition to secondary school may pose challenges due to the complexity of the curriculum and social expectations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome generally attend mainstream primary schools but may require specialized support in secondary settings.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections and requires vaccinations against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Respiratory infections are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of a functional variant in the ANKRD11 gene, which impairs the production of functional proteins essential for normal immune function.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of congenital heart defects, specifically a valve anomaly requiring regular follow-up appointments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiovascular anomalies are frequent in KBG syndrome, including structural abnormalities of the heart valves and potential septal defects. Regular cardiovascular assessments are crucial for early detection and management of complications.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which impacts her dietary habits and overall comfort level.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Constipation is a common gastrointestinal issue in KBG syndrome due to the functional variant in the ANKRD11 gene affecting gut motility and absorption.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires vaccinations against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b due to her compromised immune system.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome have a heightened susceptibility to infectious diseases due to impaired immune function, necessitating routine immunizations to protect against common bacterial infections.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits challenges with fatigue and coordination, impacting her participation in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurological manifestations in KBG syndrome include reduced stamina and difficulty maintaining balance, which can limit physical capabilities and social interactions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hearing difficulties, requiring regular audiometric checks and consideration for hearing aids or cochlear implants.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Sensorineural hearing loss is a hallmark of KBG syndrome, contributing to communication barriers and social isolation.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient faces ocular concerns such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia), which impact her visual acuity and comfort while engaging in outdoor play.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision-related issues are prevalent in KBG syndrome, including refractive errors like myopia and astigmatism, which can hinder academic performance and recreational activities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays skin characteristics such as eczema and sensitivity to sunlight, which require dermatological care and sun protection measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skin vulnerabilities are common in KBG syndrome, characterized by dryness, inflammation, and photosensitivity, underscoring the importance of skincare routines and protective behaviors.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and fragility, necessitating meticulous oral hygiene practices and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues are frequent in KBG syndrome, involving weak enamel and susceptibility to cavities, emphasizing the necessity for comprehensive dental care.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional educational support, particularly in areas related to fine motor skills and cognitive development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require tailored educational approaches to accommodate their unique learning profiles and behavioral differences.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows behavioral traits consistent with the syndrome, including autistic-like behaviors and executive function delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral manifestations in KBG syndrome encompass a spectrum of characteristics, including repetitive behaviors, sensory sensitivities, and challenges with planning and organization.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, impacting her hand and foot structures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal features in KBG syndrome include short fingers (brachydactyly) and curved fifth fingers (clinodactyly), highlighting the need for orthodontic interventions and regular skeletal evaluations.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Vaccinations: Continue to vaccinate against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b to prevent respiratory tract infections.
b) Hearing: Maintain regular hearing screenings to address potential hearing impairments and consider fitting hearing aids or cochlear implants as indicated.
c) Teeth: Encourage proper oral hygiene and schedule dental visits every six months to monitor tooth strength and prevent fractures.
d) Heart: Follow-up with cardiologists for ongoing evaluation and management of valve anomalies and other cardiac concerns.
e) Tethered Cord: Conduct MRI scans annually to assess for tethered cord syndrome, especially if sacral dimples are noted.
f) Palate: Refer for specialist review if there are persistent feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
g) Feeding: Work closely with pediatricians and dietitians to develop a personalized feeding plan that accommodates her specific needs.
h) Cardiac: Continue monitoring for potential complications associated with heart valve anomalies and structural heart defects.
i) Bowel: Implement a structured toileting program to address constipation and maintain digestive health.
j) Behaviour: Address behavioral concerns through therapeutic intervention, considering the neurodevelopmental aspects of KBG syndrome.
k) Growth: Monitor height and weight trajectories, and refer for endocrine assessment if growth patterns deviate significantly from expectations.
l) Immunization: Maintain current vaccination schedules to bolster the immune system and prevent opportunistic infections.
m) Orthodontics: Schedule regular orthodontic evaluations to address dental issues and promote optimal oral health.
n) Physical Therapy: Engage in targeted physical therapy sessions to enhance motor skills, reduce fatigue, and improve overall functionality.
o) Occupational Therapy: Collaborate with OTs to facilitate independent living skills and maximize daily activities.
p) Speech Therapy: Consult with speech therapists to address speech delays and refine communication abilities.
q) Behavioural Interventions: Utilize behavior modification techniques and counseling programs to manage challenging behaviors effectively.
r) Monitoring: Keep a close watch for emerging medical concerns and promptly address any new symptoms or developments.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing respiratory infections, particularly pneumonia. Management includes maintaining good hygiene practices, ensuring adequate hydration, and timely administration of antibiotics as prescribed by a pediatrician.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of a ventricular septal defect (VSD) requiring regular follow-up with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, including VSD, patent ductus arteriosus, and pulmonary stenosis. Regular cardiovascular assessments are crucial to monitor for potential complications and ensure appropriate treatment.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences feeding difficulties and occasional vomiting, which can lead to nutritional deficiencies and delayed growth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly have gastrointestinal issues, including feeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and constipation. Monitoring and managing these symptoms is essential for optimal nutrition and growth.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires immunizations according to the standard schedule recommended for her age group, given her increased susceptibility to infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at a higher risk of developing autoimmune diseases and allergies. Regular immunization schedules and close monitoring by a pediatrician are vital for preventing vaccine-preventable illnesses and allergic reactions.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and anxiety, which impact her social interactions and academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are common in children with KBG syndrome, affecting various aspects of their lives, including social behavior, emotional regulation, and academic achievement. Early intervention and targeted therapies can improve outcomes.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of recurrent otitis media and glue ear, necessitating frequent audiologic evaluations and possible grommet insertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are susceptible to recurrent ear infections, which can lead to hearing loss and speech delays. Regular ENT consultations and appropriate interventions are critical for managing these issues.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires regular ophthalmological examinations to monitor for vision-related issues such as astigmatism and refractive errors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems are relatively common in children with KBG syndrome, including myopia, hypermetropia, and presbyopia. Ongoing ocular health surveillance is essential for early detection and management of visual impairments.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a characteristic facial appearance characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows that sometimes fuse together (synophrys).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The facial features associated with KBG syndrome are highly distinctive and can vary in severity among affected individuals. Regular dermatological evaluations are important for identifying and managing skin conditions that may develop.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires additional dental care due to tooth size and shape variations, as well as heightened sensitivity to sugary foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues are frequent in children with KBG syndrome, including enlarged permanent teeth (macrodontia), weak enamel, and susceptibility to caries. Comprehensive dental care tailored to the patient’s unique requirements is essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient benefits from specialized educational programs and accommodations to address her cognitive and behavioral challenges, allowing her to access mainstream education while receiving the necessary support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education strategies for children with KBG syndrome focus on fostering independence, promoting social interaction, and providing opportunities for physical activity and play. Tailored educational approaches and ongoing assessment are crucial for optimizing learning outcomes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient displays behavioral differences, including ADHD, anxiety, and autistic traits, impacting her ability to engage in peer activities and adapt to new environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral and developmental differences are universal characteristics of KBG syndrome, influencing various facets of a child’s life, including social interactions, emotional expression, and coping mechanisms. Early identification and targeted therapeutic interventions can significantly enhance quality of life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has brachydactyly, characterized by shortened fingers, and clinodactyly, resulting in inward-curving of the fifth finger.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal abnormalities, such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, are frequent in children with KBG syndrome. Regular orthopedic evaluations and corrective surgeries may be necessary to address functional limitations and improve joint flexibility.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Immunizations:
- Continue to follow the standard immunization schedule recommended for her age group, given her increased susceptibility to infections.
b) Cardiovascular:
- Maintain regular follow-up with a cardiologist to monitor for potential complications of the ventricular septal defect (VSD) and other heart conditions.
c) Dentistry:
- Schedule regular dental appointments to address tooth size and shape variations, weakened enamel, and heightened sensitivity to sugary foods and drinks.
d) Vision:
- Conduct regular audiologic evaluations and consider grommet insertion for recurrent otitis media and glue ear.
e) Ear-nose-throat:
- Monitor for vision-related issues such as astigmatism and refractive errors.
f) Dermatology:
- Keep an eye on any skin changes or irregularities that may indicate underlying systemic conditions.
g) Orthodontics:
- Address tooth size and shape variations through comprehensive orthodontic evaluation and corrective measures as needed.
h) Speech Therapy:
- Work closely with speech therapists to address communication delays and provide targeted interventions to aid in verbal expression and articulation.
i) Nutritional Support:
- Ensure a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals to promote healthy growth and development.
j) Exercise:
- Encourage participation in physical activities suitable for her age and abilities to maintain strength and coordination.
k) Behavioural Interventions:
- Implement targeted behavioral therapies and support systems to address ADHD, anxiety, and other behavioral differences.
l) Social Interaction:
- Foster opportunities for social engagement and encourage friendships through community events and extracurricular activities.
m) Academic Accommodations:
- Seek educational accommodations and resources to facilitate her learning and maximize her potential in mainstream settings.
n) Medical Follow-Ups:
- Regular visits to specialists to monitor for any emerging medical concerns and address them promptly.
o) Genetic Counseling:
- Consider genetic counseling sessions to discuss the implications of the ANKRD11 gene variant and future reproductive options.
p) Endocrine Evaluation:
- Given the high prevalence of hormonal imbalances in KBG syndrome, consider periodic endocrine evaluations to rule out thyroid dysfunction, growth hormone deficiency, and other endocrine-related issues.
q) Vestibular Rehabilitation:
- Explore vestibular rehabilitation techniques to address balance and dizziness concerns, especially if the patient experiences difficulty with physical activities.
r) Sleep Disorders:
- Monitor for sleep apnea or restless leg syndrome, which can exacerbate existing behavioral and developmental challenges.
s) Neurodevelopmental Assessments:
- Regular neurodevelopmental assessments to track progress and identify areas for further intervention.
t) Psychological Support:
- Offer psychological support and counseling services to help the patient cope with the emotional and behavioral challenges associated with KBG syndrome.
u) Family Support Groups:
- Encourage involvement in local support groups for families of children with KBG syndrome to share experiences and receive valuable insights from others facing similar challenges.
v) Long-Term Surveillance:
- Continuously monitor for the emergence of novel medical concerns and implement proactive screening protocols as needed.
w) Parental Education:
- Provide extensive parental education on the syndrome, its manifestations, and best practices for managing the patient’s specific needs.
x) Multidisciplinary Team Approach:
- Utilize a multidisciplinary team approach involving pediatricians, neurologists, speech therapists, psychologists, orthodontists, and other specialists to tailor a holistic care plan.
y) Continuous Improvement:
- Regularly review and refine the care plan based on the patient’s evolving needs and the latest advancements in medical knowledge and treatment modalities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has experienced occasional respiratory infections, primarily viral colds and bronchitis. These have generally responded well to standard antibiotic treatments and supportive care.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Respiratory tract infections are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of a functional copy of the ANKRD11 gene. While most children recover fully, some may experience more frequent or severe episodes compared to those without the condition.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has a history of a congenital heart defect, specifically a ventricular septal defect (VSD). This requires ongoing monitoring and follow-up with cardiologists to assess the size and impact of the defect over time.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Individuals with KBG syndrome are predisposed to congenital heart defects due to the functional copy of the ANKRD11 gene. Ventricular septal defects are among the most commonly encountered heart abnormalities in this population. Regular cardiovascular assessments are crucial to monitor the health of the heart and ensure timely intervention if any issues arise.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child experiences difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and regurgitation, which can lead to aspiration pneumonia. These issues necessitate dietary modifications and careful mealtime supervision to minimize choking risks.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Difficulty swallowing and regurgitation are common challenges faced by individuals with KBG syndrome due to the anatomical and physiological effects of the ANKRD11 gene variant. Management strategies, including dietary restrictions and careful meal planning, are essential to maintain overall digestive health.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has a history of seizures, which were initially managed with anticonvulsants. Given the variability in seizure frequency and type, continued monitoring and consideration of alternative therapies may be warranted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Seizure activity is a concerning aspect of KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 20-40% of individuals. The management of seizures involves a tailored approach based on the specific presentation and response to initial treatments. Continued surveillance and flexibility in therapeutic approaches are critical components of managing seizure control in this population.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child exhibits behavioral differences, including characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). These behaviors contribute to social interactions and academic performance challenges.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral differences are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, encompassing a range of traits associated with ASD and ADHD. These neurodevelopmental factors significantly influence social behavior, cognitive abilities, and executive functions, impacting various aspects of daily life.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:

Ongoing management strategies, including regular ENT evaluations and proactive interventions like grommet insertion and hearing aid use, are vital for maintaining auditory health.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has a history of vision-related issues, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia). Regular eye examinations are recommended to track visual development and adjust prescription as necessary.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Vision impairments are prevalent in KBG syndrome, characterized by astigmatism and myopia. Ongoing ocular assessment and adjustment of corrective lenses are essential to optimize visual function and prevent further deterioration.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child displays a distinctive facial appearance, including a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows. These features are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
The characteristic facial features observed in KBG syndrome are highly indicative of the condition. These phenotypic markers provide valuable diagnostic clues and serve as a foundation for understanding the broader implications of the genetic variation.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child attends a mainstream primary school but requires additional support to meet the diverse needs of his peers. He benefits from structured play-based activities, adapted curriculum materials, and targeted educational interventions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Education outcomes for individuals with KBG syndrome vary widely depending on the severity of their developmental delays and behavioral differences. Mainstream schooling provides opportunities for peer interaction and skill acquisition, while accommodations tailored to specific needs are crucial for fostering optimal learning environments.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child demonstrates behavioral differences, including characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD. These behavioral manifestations impact his social interactions, emotional regulation, and academic performance.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Behavioral differences are pervasive in KBG syndrome, manifesting as elements of ASD and ADHD. These behavioral traits profoundly influence social dynamics, emotional expression, and cognitive capabilities, shaping the lived experiences of individuals with the condition.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
Our child has an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis), which requires periodic monitoring and possible orthopedic interventions to manage the condition effectively.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Spinal deformities, particularly scoliosis, are frequent complications in individuals with KBG syndrome. Ongoing surveillance and consideration of appropriate management strategies are vital for ensuring long-term health and quality of life.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Seizures:
Continue monitoring and adjusting anticonvulsant medications as necessary. Encourage adherence to prescribed dosages and attend scheduled clinic visits for reassessment.

b) Hearing:
Maintain regular audiometric checks to monitor hearing thresholds and adjust hearing aids or cochlear implants as required. Address any concerns regarding speech development promptly.

c) Vision:
Prescribe and periodically review spectacles or contact lenses to optimize visual clarity and comfort. Schedule comprehensive eye exams every six months to track visual development.

d) Heart:
Continue follow-up with cardiologists to monitor the size and impact of the ventricular septal defect. Consider echocardiograms and ECGs annually to detect any changes or complications.

e) Tethered Cord:
If clinical concerns arise, arrange MRI scans to evaluate the tethered cord condition. Follow-up consultations with pediatric neurosurgeons may be necessary for definitive management decisions.

f) Palate:
Refer for specialist review if persistent feeding difficulties or speech concerns are noted. Consider surgical evaluation if there are unresolved palate anomalies.

g) Dental:
Encourage regular dental check-ups and implement a rigorous home-care regimen to prevent cavities and gum disease. Refer for orthodontic evaluation if necessary.

h) Cardiologist Consultations:
Schedule annual cardiology appointments to monitor the heart condition and discuss any emerging concerns. Consider referral to a pediatric cardiologist for specialized care.

i) Orthopedic Review:
Arrange a skeletal review (wrist X-ray, hip, spine, and skull X-rays) in children following diagnosis. Consider follow-up appointments with orthopedic experts for guidance on managing scoliosis and other musculoskeletal issues.

j) Neurology Follow-Up:
Engage with a multidisciplinary team specializing in neurology to address behavioral and developmental concerns. Explore options for behavioral therapy and educational support.

k) Endocrinology Evaluation:
Consider referral for endocrine investigations if height remains below the 2nd percentile. Evaluate thyroid function, growth hormone levels, and other relevant parameters to rule out hormonal imbalances.

l) Immunology Monitoring:
Continue immunological assessments to monitor seizure control and vaccine responsiveness. Discuss the necessity of vaccinations and the timing of booster doses with a pediatric immunologist.

m) Behavioral Therapy:
Initiate and maintain behavioral therapy programs tailored to the child’s specific needs. Collaborate with psychologists and therapists to develop effective strategies for managing behavioral differences.

n) Occupational Therapy:
Implement a structured OT program focusing on fine motor skills, adaptive techniques, and daily living skills. Work closely with OT practitioners to tailor interventions to the child’s requirements.

o) Speech Therapy:
Engage in speech therapy sessions to address feeding difficulties, speech delay, and communication barriers. Develop personalized treatment plans and monitor progress regularly.

p) Physical Therapy:
Consider physical therapy evaluations to address mobility limitations and promote overall physical fitness. Tailored exercise regimes and mobility aids may be beneficial.

q) Nutritional Support:
Provide a balanced diet rich in vitamins, minerals, and protein to support healthy growth and development. Monitor nutrient intake and adjust accordingly based on consultation with a nutritionist.

r) Parental Education:
Offer workshops and seminars for parents to educate them on managing the specific challenges faced by their child. Share best practices and coping strategies for dealing with behavioral and developmental issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: She has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away. We've gotten her glasses to help correct this, and it's made a big difference in her ability to see the board at school and read books comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she doesn't respond right away when we call her name. It's like she's not hearing us or is too focused on what she's doing to notice. This has been a bit of a concern for us because we worry she might be missing important instructions or warnings.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods can be a challenge for her. She tends to avoid meats and tougher vegetables because they hurt her teeth or are hard to bite through. We've had to adapt meal times to include softer options or cut her food into smaller pieces to make eating easier.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, there's an issue with one of the valves in her heart. Regular check-ups with the cardiologist have become a routine part of our lives now. So far, everything has been stable, but we remain vigilant for any changes or signs that something might be off.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Occasionally, she'll have these episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't seem to be with us anymore. These blank spells can be alarming because we never know when they might happen or how long they'll last. It's been a point of discussion with her neurologist to understand and manage these episodes better.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a significant issue. She has a strong aversion to certain tastes and textures, which limits her diet considerably. Mealtime can sometimes feel like a battle because of this, trying to find foods she'll eat without gagging or pushing them away.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the heart valve issue and feeding difficulties, we've also noticed she struggles with speech clarity. There are moments when her words aren't clear or she seems to jumble them together. Additionally, there are palatal abnormalities we're keeping an eye on. These various challenges require close monitoring and regular visits to several specialists to ensure we're doing everything possible to support her health and development.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections and requires vaccinations against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Respiratory infections are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the weakened immune system and susceptibility to bacterial infections.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of cardiovascular issues, including a previous episode of transient ischemic attack (TIA) and a recent echocardiogram indicating left ventricular hypertrophy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiovascular complications are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of ANKRD11 mutations, which can lead to structural abnormalities and functional impairments in the heart.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and constipation, which are commonly associated with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: GERD and constipation are frequent gastrointestinal complaints in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the underlying genetic mutation affecting gastrointestinal motility and peristalsis.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a compromised immune system, requiring immunizations and prophylactic antibiotics for infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome generally have a weaker immune response compared to the general population, necessitating additional precautions against infectious diseases.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are a known complication of KBG syndrome due to the ANKRD11 gene mutation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Seizures are a common occurrence in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic predisposition towards neuronal dysfunction and excitotoxicity.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient suffers from conductive hearing loss and nasal congestion, which can exacerbate sinusitis and other respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Conductive hearing loss is a hallmark feature of KBG syndrome due to the genetic alteration impacting outer and middle ear structures.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of vision-related issues, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia), which are common among individuals with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, particularly refractive errors, are frequently encountered in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic mutation affecting ocular development.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits dermatological manifestations such as eczema and skin pigmentation variations, which are not uncommon in individuals with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skin conditions, including eczema and hypopigmented macules, are frequently observed in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic alteration influencing melanocyte function.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient faces challenges with tooth eruption and potential dental trauma, given the anatomical and physiological alterations resulting from the ANKRD11 gene mutation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues, such as delayed tooth eruption and susceptibility to dental injuries, are typical concerns in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic factor affecting craniofacial development.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires specialized educational interventions due to cognitive delays, behavioral differences, and sensory processing needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require tailored educational approaches to accommodate their unique learning profiles and behavioral characteristics.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays behavioral differences, including autistic traits, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, which impact social interactions and academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral and developmental differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, are frequently observed in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic mutation altering neural connectivity and neurotransmission.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient presents with skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), which contribute to overall physical development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal features, such as short fingers and abnormal joint formation, are consistent observations in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the genetic alteration affecting cartilage development and bone structure.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Immunizations: Continue routine vaccinations, including pneumococcal and Hib vaccines, to protect against infections.
b) Anticonvulsants: Maintain current antiepileptic drug regimen to control seizures and reduce seizure frequency.
c) Hearing Monitoring: Regular audiometric evaluations to address hearing loss and ensure proper auditory development.
d) Orthodontics: Consult with an orthodontist to address potential dental issues and promote optimal oral health.
e) Cardiology Follow-Up: Regular cardiac assessments to monitor for arrhythmias, valve issues, or structural abnormalities.
f) Vestibular Therapy: Consider vestibular rehabilitation to address balance and coordination deficits.
g) Speech Therapy: Continue ongoing speech therapy sessions to aid in language development and articulation.
h) Occupational Therapy: Implement targeted OT strategies to enhance fine motor skills, self-care abilities, and daily living activities.
i) Physical Therapy: Engage in regular PT programs to improve strength, flexibility, and mobility.
j) Behavioural Interventions: Collaborate with a psychologist or behavior therapist to develop and implement therapeutic plans addressing behavioral concerns.
k) Nutritional Support: Work with a pediatric dietitian to tailor feeding regimens and provide nutritional counseling.
l) Epilepsy Management: Review and adjust antiepileptic medications based on seizure patterns and tolerability.
m) Endocrine Evaluation: Consider thyroid function testing and other hormonal assessments as indicated.
n) Genetic Counseling: Discuss options for carrier screening and prenatal testing for future pregnancies.
o) Craniofacial Surgery: Evaluate the need for corrective surgeries, such as palatoplasty, to address feeding difficulties and speech impediments.
p) Tethered Cord Assessment: Perform MRI scans to evaluate for tethered cord syndrome and initiate treatment if necessary.
q) Sacral Dimple Observation: Keep a watchful eye for sacral dimple development and consider surgical intervention if concerns arise.
r) Growth Hormone Considerations: Further investigate the use of GH therapy in managing growth velocity and height outcomes.
s) Dental Prophylaxis: Schedule comprehensive dental cleanings and fluoride treatments to maintain oral hygiene and prevent cavities.
t) Ophthalmology Reviews: Regular ophthalmologic examinations to address vision and ocular surface integrity.
u) Cardiac Surveillance: Continue annual echocardiograms and EKGs to monitor cardiac status and detect early signs of structural or functional abnormalities.
v) Neurodevelopmental Evaluations: Regular neuropsychological assessments to track cognitive, behavioral, and adaptive skill progress.
w) Audiometry: Reassess hearing thresholds annually to monitor for fluctuation and optimize hearing management.
x) Feeding Modifications: Continuously refine feeding techniques and explore alternative feeding methods to optimize intake and minimize risk of aspiration.
y) Sleep Studies: Consider polysomnography to assess sleep architecture and identify potential sleep-related breathing disorders.
z) Gluten-Free/Dairy-Free Diet: Explore the benefits of gluten-free/dairy-free diets for select patients with suspected food sensitivities or intolerances.
aa) Vitamin D Supplementation: Ensure adequate vitamin D levels through supplementation and sun exposure.

a) How this affects the patient:
- Delayed gastric emptying leading to poor appetite and frequent feedings
- Risk of aspiration pneumonia
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Increased risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
- Potential for delayed gastric emptying

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:

- Potential for autoimmune reactions

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

a) How this affects the patient:

- Increased sensitivity to cold temperatures
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

- Common occurrence of similar skeletal features

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences occasional respiratory infections and requires vaccinations against influenza and pneumococcus.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to developing respiratory tract infections, which can lead to hospitalization and prolonged illness episodes. Vaccinations against influenza and pneumococcus are crucial to prevent complications such as pneumonia and sepsis.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a history of transient ischemic attacks (TIAs) and carotid artery stenosis, indicating cardiovascular risk factors.
- The presence of TIAs suggests a predisposition towards vascular events, warranting close monitoring and consideration of preventive measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing cardiovascular diseases due to the underlying genetic mutation affecting ANKRD11. Regular cardiovascular assessments, including echocardiograms and lipid profile monitoring, are essential to detect and manage potential issues early.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and constipation, impacting dietary habits and overall nutrition.
- Management strategies, including dietary modifications and possible use of proton pump inhibitors, are recommended to alleviate symptoms and promote better digestion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly suffer from GERD, which can lead to nutritional deficiencies and delayed growth. Proton pump inhibitors and dietary adjustments are effective in managing this condition.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a weakened immune system, increasing susceptibility to infections.
- Regular immunizations, particularly against influenza and pneumococcus, are critical to protect against vaccine-preventable illnesses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at heightened risk of developing autoimmune disorders due to the genetic alteration in ANKRD11. Annual immunizations and periodic blood tests to monitor antibody levels are advisable.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient displays behavioral differences, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and anxiety.
- Behavioral interventions, such as behavior therapy and medication (if necessary), are beneficial in managing these challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit behavioral traits similar to those observed in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD. Early intervention programs targeting behavioral management can provide significant benefits.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient suffers from conductive hearing loss, requiring frequent audiometric evaluations.
- Speech therapy and hearing aids are recommended to optimize communication abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Conductive hearing loss is a common feature in KBG syndrome, contributing to speech delays and difficulty in social interactions. Audiological assessments and appropriate interventions are vital for improving auditory function.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has ocular manifestations such as squint and astigmatism, necessitating regular ophthalmologic examinations.
- Vision correction, including spectacles and possibly orthokeratology lenses, can improve visual acuity and comfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Ocular abnormalities are relatively common in KBG syndrome, potentially leading to amblyopia and refractive errors. Comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluations are essential to address these concerns promptly.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient presents with skin findings such as eczema and ichthyosis-like dermatoses.
- Skin care routines, including moisturizing and avoiding irritants, are crucial for maintaining skin health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome often exhibit dermatological features such as eczema and ichthyosis, which can impact quality of life. Gentle skincare practices and adherence to prescribed regimens are key to managing these conditions effectively.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has dental issues such as weak tooth enamel and bruxism (teeth grinding).
- Dental hygiene protocols, fluoride treatment, and orthodontic considerations are essential to maintain oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental problems are frequent in KBG syndrome, including weak tooth enamel and bruxism. Regular dental check-ups and appropriate restorative and preventive measures are imperative for preserving oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires additional educational support to cope with academic demands.
- Special educational needs (SEN) planning, including provision of an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), is necessary to meet the unique educational needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently require tailored educational approaches to accommodate their cognitive and physical limitations. Provision of an EHCP ensures access to the requisite support and resources to facilitate optimal educational outcomes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient shows behavioral differences, including ASD-like characteristics and anxiety.
- Behavioral therapies, such as applied behavior analysis (ABA) and mindfulness-based interventions, can aid in managing behavioral challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently display behaviors reminiscent of those observed in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and anxiety. Evidence-based behavioral interventions, such as ABA and mindfulness-based techniques, can significantly enhance emotional regulation and social interaction.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, influencing hand and foot morphology.
- Orthopedic surveillance, including X-rays and biomechanical assessments, is advised to monitor bone development and identify potential issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal features are common in KBG syndrome, contributing to limb length discrepancies and joint flexibility constraints. Regular skeletal assessments, including X-rays and biomechanical analyses, are essential for timely identification and management of associated musculoskeletal concerns.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- **Vaccinations:** Continue routine vaccinations against influenza and pneumococcus, ensuring compliance with current guidelines.
- **Heart Monitoring:** Regular echocardiograms and ECGs are recommended to monitor cardiovascular status and detect any emerging issues.
- **Behavior Therapy:** Implement comprehensive behavioral therapy programs, incorporating ABA and mindfulness-based interventions, to address behavioral differences and anxiety.
- **Orthodontics:** Consider orthodontic evaluation and treatment options to correct dental arch dimensions and address bite alignment.
- **Speech Therapy:** Engage speech therapists to develop targeted therapeutic plans focusing on speech articulation, volume control, and pragmatic language skills.
- **Nutrition Support:** Encourage a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals, especially calcium and vitamin D, to support bone health and overall growth.
- **Physical Activity:** Promote regular physical activity, emphasizing gentle activities suitable for the patient’s capabilities, to foster motor skill development and improve overall fitness.
- **Monitoring Growth:** Maintain vigilance regarding height and weight percentile tracking, considering referral for endocrine investigations if concerns persist.
- **Referral for Review:** Promptly refer the patient for pediatric craniofacial assessment if squint, palate issues, or feeding difficulties are persistent or severe.
- **Cardiac Surveillance:** Follow-up with cardiologists for ongoing cardiac monitoring, including echocardiograms and ECGs, to ensure continued safety and wellbeing.
- **Neurological Assessment:** Schedule neurodevelopmental assessments periodically to track progress and adjust support strategies as necessary.
- **Eye Examination:** Arrange comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluations annually to monitor for any evolving ocular issues.
- **Skin Care:** Adhere to a consistent skincare regimen, utilizing gentle cleansers and hydrating products, to maintain skin integrity and reduce irritation.
- **Dental Care:** Implement stringent dental hygiene protocols, including fluoride treatments and orthodontic consultations, to safeguard oral health.
- **Educational Planning:** Develop an EHCP plan tailored to the patient’s specific needs, encompassing provisions for SEN, assistive technology, and specialized teaching methods.
- **Behavioral Interventions:** Initiate and refine behavioral therapy programs, integrating ABA and mindfulness-based techniques, to address behavioral challenges comprehensively.
- **Bone Density Studies:** Consider bone density assessments, particularly in children with larger-than-average permanent teeth, to mitigate the risk of osteoporosis later in life.
- **Musculoskeletal Surveillance:** Perform X-ray and biomechanical analyses periodically to monitor bone development and detect any latent skeletal issues.
- **Psychosocial Support:** Offer psychosocial counseling and peer support groups to help the patient and their family navigate the multifaceted challenges of living with KBG syndrome.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences difficulty seeing clearly while reading, particularly with cold foods and drinks.
- The patient has episodes of seizures requiring medication to control them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly have issues with vision, including blurry vision and sensitivity to light.
- They may develop otitis media or glue ear, leading to temporary hearing loss and frequent need for ear tubes.
- Some have feeding difficulties and vomiting, affecting their nutritional intake and overall health.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient requires regular cardiology check-ups to ensure their heart is healthy.
- One of the patient's concerns is the presence of a tethered cord, which needs further investigation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Heart conditions are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with studies reporting rates ranging from 15%-40%.
- Tethered cord syndrome is also a concern, potentially causing pain, weakness, and other complications.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient struggles with eating, often refusing food and experiencing vomiting.
- Cold foods and drinks exacerbate the issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome frequently encounter feeding difficulties and gastroenterological issues, such as reflux and occasional stomach upset.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient takes medication to control seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Seizure management is crucial for individuals with KBG syndrome, as it can lead to various complications if left untreated.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient experiences seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Seizures are a common occurrence in KBG syndrome, impacting cognitive functions and behavior.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has a delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle.
- Cold foods and drinks cause discomfort in the ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle is a known feature of KBG syndrome.
- Exposure to cold temperatures can trigger ear infections and discomfort.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has vision-related issues, including astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia/hypermetropia).
- The patient experiences sensitivity to cold temperatures in the ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems are quite common in individuals with KBG syndrome, affecting activities like reading and watching TV.
- Sensitivity to cold temperatures in the ears is a noted symptom.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has dental issues, including weak enamel and sensitivity to cold foods/drinks.
- The patient requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental problems are frequent in KBG syndrome, including tooth sensitivity and potential enamel weakness.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient attends mainstream primary school but faces challenges with academic performance and social interactions.
- The patient benefits from additional educational support and may require accommodations in secondary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some excelling academically and others needing more support.
- Specialized settings or continued mainstream education with adaptations can provide suitable environments for many.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
- The patient shows delays in certain developmental milestones, such as fine motor skills and speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, contributing to challenges in areas like social interaction and self-regulation.
- ASD, ADHD, and anxiety are frequently reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
- The patient has skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger).
- An unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis) is occasionally observed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal abnormalities are a consistent feature of KBG syndrome, influencing posture, movement, and joint flexibility.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups are essential for maintaining oral health.
- Monitoring the positioning of the testes in boys is recommended to address potential undescended testes.
- Ophthalmology evaluations should be conducted regularly to monitor vision and address any vision-related issues promptly.
- Cardiologists should perform thorough examinations and recommend appropriate interventions based on the patient's specific condition.
- Given the prevalence of tethered cord syndrome, consideration should be given to MRI scans for infants and young children with suspected tethered cord.
- Regular physical examinations and X-rays of the wrist, hips, spine, and skull are advised to assess skeletal development and detect any anomalies early.
- Management of seizures should involve a multidisciplinary approach, possibly involving neurologists, pediatricians, and psychiatrists.
- Speech therapy and occupational therapy can play a vital role in helping the patient overcome communication barriers and improve daily living skills.
- Behavioral therapy might assist in managing behavioral differences and improving social interactions.
- Nutritional counseling tailored to the patient's specific dietary restrictions and swallowing concerns is advisable.
- Family support groups and educational resources can offer invaluable guidance and coping strategies for caregivers and siblings.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects her ability to see distant objects clearly and requires constant monitoring and corrective measures to prevent further complications. We've been working closely with her ophthalmologist to manage this condition effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child often asks people to repeat themselves because she can't seem to catch everything the first time. It's not that she can't hear, but rather that she struggles with processing auditory information quickly. This has led to some frustrations in communication, especially in noisy environments where it's harder for her to focus.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods has proven challenging for our daughter due to some dental issues we're still trying to fully understand. Her dentist thinks it might be related to the alignment of her teeth or possibly an issue with her jaw. We're exploring orthodontic options to address these difficulties and make eating easier for her.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physical activities that last for extended periods are particularly taxing for our daughter. She tires easily and can't keep up with her peers during playtime or sports. Cardiologists have noted some concerns regarding her heart's efficiency in pumping blood under stress or exertion. We're managing this with regular exercise tailored to her needs and close supervision from healthcare professionals.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.
